The verdicts for the visible geometry (shallow circular shape, sloped sides) and material (black non-stick/seasoned surface with oil sheen) are accurate and align with the visual evidence. The Router was not too lenient; it appropriately marked occluded features as 'is_testable: false' rather than guessing.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies in the food (waxy/smooth) and structural issues with the spatula (indistinct head/fusion). The Perceptual Quality Auditor detected slight noise but missed the structural/textural nuances. The Topology Boundary Auditor provided a mask confidence of ~0.81, which is moderate but not definitive proof of clean boundaries given the complex overlap of food items. I agree with the Router's assessment of the food texture being 'waxy' (Severity 2.5) and the spatula having minor fusion/definition issues (Severity 1.5). These are classic AI artifacts in cooking scenes. The severity ratings are appropriate; they are noticeable upon inspection but do not completely destroy the illusion of the scene.
alignment_reasoning: The image strongly conforms to the 'frying pan' class. The Fine Grained Classifier confirmed this with high confidence (Logit 7.05 vs 5.82 for Wok). All testable checkpoints regarding geometry and material passed. The missing handle does not detract from the class identity as the core functional component (the pan body) is clearly present and correct.
artifact_reasoning: While the pan itself is structurally sound, the contents (food and spatula) exhibit AI-generation artifacts. The food lacks realistic fibrous texture, appearing waxy or smudged (Router Severity 2.5). The wooden spatula has soft, ill-defined edges where it meets the food, suggesting minor fusion (Router Severity 1.5). These artifacts lower the overall quality score significantly below a perfect 5.0, as they break the photorealism of the macro shot.
